guard: pinned teardown refuses reused pids and torn pins; win32 launches write a creation-time pin; a legacy live record warns and remains signalable only when no sibling pin exists
why: M1 breaks the shared verdict (the mismatch comparison in verifyIdentityPin) and must redden
the DELIVERY cell A1, whose refusal is the direct measurement of the pre-fix defect. The
delivery teardown has no gate of its own: it is down's stopLocalProcess, so A1 reddening under
M1 is its route through the seam. Mismatch protection is the guarded property; legacy no-pin
records deliberately warn and proceed for upgrade compatibility.
M1 IS THE ONE COMPARISON THE DESIGN TURNS ON, in the workspace seam all four teardown paths
share (stopManager, stopDelivery, stopAuthService, and down's stopLocalProcess for the broker
and web). Folding it to match makes every pinned record pass verification, which is precisely
the bare-pid behaviour the issue forbids. B1/B3/B5 redden too, but A1 is named because its
refusal is the exact shape the live repro killed a foreign process through.
M3 RESTORES THE #1437 WIN32 DEFECT: identityStartToken returns undefined on win32, so a launch
never has a token to pin. F1 is the off-Windows executable of that branch.
M4 RESTORES THE WRITE SKIP: writeIdentityPin returns without creating a sibling even when a
token exists. That is the Windows steady state the issue named. F2 must red.
Build workspace and its dependencies for the baseline, then only workspace per mutant.
Invoke the suite directly: smoke:pid-identity also builds and would repeat that work.
afterRestore rebuilds workspace because git cannot recover a compiled mutant in ignored dist.

mutations.name: M1 the shared verdict stops reporting mismatch (verifyIdentityPin folded to match)
mutations.find: return live === record.token ? { kind: "match" } : { kind: "mismatch", liveToken: live };
mutations.expectRed: A1 a REUSED pid (pin mismatch) is REFUSED by stopDelivery, never signalled
mutations.cell: A1 a REUSED pid (pin mismatch) is REFUSED by stopDelivery, never signalled
mutations.note: The one comparison the whole design turns on. Folding it to match makes every pinned record pass verification, which is precisely the bare-pid behaviour the issue forbids; A1 goes red the moment the signal is sent.

mutations.name: M3 win32 identity token is undefined again (the #1437 reader defect)
mutations.expectRed: F1 win32 identity uses the creation-time reader, not undefined
mutations.cell: F1 win32 identity uses the creation-time reader, not undefined
mutations.note: The Windows reader branch must not fold to undefined. F1 injects a FILETIME reader and names win32; returning undefined is the pre-fix processStartToken behaviour.

mutations.name: M4 writeIdentityPin never writes a sibling (the #1437 pin-absent defect)
mutations.expectRed: F2 a win32 launch WRITES the sibling pin (the #1437 defect is writing none)
mutations.cell: F2 a win32 launch WRITES the sibling pin (the #1437 defect is writing none)
mutations.note: Restores the write skip that made every Windows record unpinned. F2 reds when the sibling is absent after a win32-capable launch.

mutations.name: M5 the bridge pin never reaches the pin path (the #1238 bridge-pin step removed)
mutations.expectRed: G2 a crash after `bridge-pin` leaves the OLD pid checked against its own line of a two-line pin (match, never legacy or torn)
mutations.cell: G2 a crash after `bridge-pin` leaves the OLD pid checked against its own line of a two-line pin (match, never legacy or torn)
mutations.note: Without the bridge, the crash planted at bridge-pin leaves the OLD single-line pin, so G2's two-line check fails. The same mutant would commit the NEW pid beside the OLD pin, a torn pairing, which is what G3 would read next.

mutations.name: M6 the bridge pin drops the old record's line (#1238)
mutations.expectRed: G2 a crash after `bridge-pin` leaves the OLD pid checked against its own line of a two-line pin (match, never legacy or torn)
mutations.cell: G2 a crash after `bridge-pin` leaves the OLD pid checked against its own line of a two-line pin (match, never legacy or torn)
mutations.note: With only the NEW line in the bridge, the OLD pid the pidfile still names has no line of its own, so G2 reads torn-pairing instead of match: the old record would lose its check for the length of the window.

mutations.name: M7 the pidfile is written in place during temporaries, never to a temporary (#1238)
mutations.expectRed: G0 a first publish with no injection leaves a complete, matching record
mutations.cell: G0 a first publish with no injection leaves a complete, matching record
mutations.note: Hand-confirmed: G0 is the FIRST writePidPair call ever made against a fresh pidfile path, so it is the call that hits the mutant first (not G1): the pidfile is written directly, then renameSync(pidTemp, pidfilePath) throws ENOENT since pidTemp was never created. G0 is try/catch-wrapped so this is now a clean, named red rather than an uncaught crash.

mutations.name: M8 a token with spaces is refused again (the #3924 two-field parse)
mutations.expectRed: P1 a start token with spaces (macOS lstart) reads back as a record
mutations.cell: P1 a start token with spaces (macOS lstart) reads back as a record
mutations.note: Restores the pre-fix rule that a record is exactly two whitespace-separated fields: a macOS lstart token reads as unattributable, which is what made the manager fail its own pin at boot and cotal down refuse every component on a Mac. P3 also reds on macOS; P1 is named because it reds on every platform.

mutations.name: M9 the token's own spacing is collapsed (a padded day no longer matches the live token)
mutations.expectRed: P2 a padded one-digit day keeps its double space byte for byte
mutations.cell: P2 a padded one-digit day keeps its double space byte for byte
mutations.note: The live token from ps keeps the double space before a one-digit day, so a parser that normalises spacing would read a pin that never matches its own process for the first nine days of every month.

mutations.name: M10 the single-record parser accepts multiple pin lines
mutations.expectRed: P4 multiple pin lines are not a single identity record
mutations.cell: P4 multiple pin lines are not a single identity record
